root_cause_label: False Premise That Configure Must Succeed Before Any Task Work Can Begin
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent adopted the false premise that fixing the ./configure SIGPIPE failure was the necessary prerequisite to the task, and never examined the actual GC source code changes, spending 335 steps in a futile configure-debugging and config.log-reading loop.
t_commit_evidence: Step 84: agent finds 'configure: caught signal 13' in config.log. Rather than pivoting to examine the GC runtime source files or git history (the actual task), the agent continues log-inspection and then enters a permanent thrashing loop re-reading the same 524-line config.log in 10-line increments for the next 251 steps. After step 84, given the agent's actual subsequent behavior, the failing outcome is irrevocably locked in.
trigger_explanation: The agent acts on the unverified assumption that ./configure must succeed before any other work can proceed. It never considers that the actual task—fixing a GC source bug that causes bootstrapping to crash—could be approached by reading git history, examining runtime/*.c changes, or understanding the code change directly, bypassing the configure obstacle. This false premise drives all 335 steps of futile configure debugging.
forewarning_evidence: configure: error: could not make ./config.status [The command completed with exit code 1.]
